name: Volkov-Saito Precision VS-O/U Sport 'Duelist'
description:
The Volkov-Saito VS-O/U Sport is a break-action over-under shotgun chambered in 12 gauge with 30-inch barrels, a single selective trigger, and an ejector system that throws spent shells clear of the action. The weapon is hand-engraved with a geometric pattern that is unique to each unit — no two Duelists bear the same engraving — and the stock is shaped from figured walnut selected for grain quality.

The Duelist is a premium sporting shotgun for competitive trap and skeet shooting, positioned at the top of the market alongside the finest sporting arms ever produced. The over-under barrel configuration provides two different choke settings in a single weapon — typically improved cylinder on the bottom barrel for close targets and modified on the top barrel for distance targets — selectable by trigger position.

Volkov-Saito produces the Duelist in their premium workshop, limited to two hundred units per year. The waiting list extends to four years, and secondary-market prices consistently exceed new-purchase prices. In the insular world of competitive clay shooting, the Duelist is the weapon against which all others are measured — not always fairly, but always inevitably.
specifications:
caliber: 12 gauge
effective_range: 50 meters (sporting loads)
rate_of_fire: Two shots (break-action reload)
magazine_capacity: 2 rounds
weight: 3.4 kg
tactical_use: No tactical application. This is a premium sporting shotgun for competitive clay shooting. The two-shot capacity and long barrels make it unsuitable for any defensive or offensive role. Its value is entirely in sporting and collectible contexts.
cultural_context: The Duelist is wealth, taste, and skill combined in steel and walnut. In the Mid and Spire social circles where competitive shooting serves as networking and status display, the Duelist is the membership card. Owning one places the holder in a community of two hundred per year — a manufactured exclusivity that Volkov-Saito manages with the precision they apply to their firearms.
story_hooks: A Duelist with unique engraving is found at a murder scene — a Φ40,000 sporting shotgun used to kill someone with birdshot at close range. The weapon is easily traceable, which suggests the killer either didn't care about being identified or intended the weapon to send a message.
The four-year waiting list for a Duelist is compromised, and the personal information of two hundred of GLMZ's wealthiest residents is leaked to criminal networks.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, elegant break-action over-under shotgun with a refined sporting profile. The long 30-inch barrels dominate the silhouette, creating a graceful upward taper from receiver to muzzle. The wood furniture gleams with figured grain patterns, giving the weapon an heirloom quality rarely seen in modern arms. Despite its lethal purpose, it reads as sculptural—more instrument than tool.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 114 cm | Barrel length: 76 cm (30 inches) | Receiver width: 8 cm | Stock length: 38 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Perfectly balanced at 3.4 kg—feels substantial but not burdensome in the hands. The weight distribution favors the barrel slightly, creating a natural pointing dynamic that encourages smooth swing transitions. Hefty enough to absorb recoil cleanly, light enough for sustained competitive shooting.
physical_description.primary_material: Steel receiver and barrels; figured walnut stock and foregrip; chrome-plated internal action components
physical_description.finish: Polished steel with a satin sheen on the barrel flats; high-gloss varnished walnut stock with oil-finished grip areas. The receiver features a deep blue-black finish with subtle hand-brushed texture marks visible under direct light.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep blue-black steel barrels, rich honey-to-chocolate figured walnut stock with natural grain variation, brushed steel trigger guard and selector lever accents
physical_description.grip_texture: Walnut stock has a smooth, oiled finish with subtle grip ridges carved into the wrist area. The foregrip features a slight palm swell with fine checkering (20 lines per inch) for secure mounting. No modern rubberized elements—all organic materials.
distinctive_features: Unique hand-engraved geometric patterns on the receiver—no two identical across all units produced
Single selective trigger with visible position indicator (small lever near trigger guard to select top or bottom barrel)
Auto-ejector system ports visible on receiver bottom—small spring-loaded gates that flip open under the action
Walnut grain figure varies dramatically across each weapon—natural wood variation as design element
Traditional drop-at-heel stock design with no tactical furniture or rails
Ventilated rib running the full length of barrels (1.2 cm wide) with bead sight at muzzle
Engraving detail extends to the inside of the action—visible when broken open
Serial number etched subtly into the barrel flats in fine script
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: "VOLKOV-SAITO PRECISION" engraved in elegant serif script on the top barrel flat near the breech. Year of manufacture (2-digit) and serial number stamped inside the action on the receiver. A maker's mark—a small geometric Volkov-Saito house symbol—appears on the trigger guard, integrated into the engraving pattern.
physical_description.condition_typical: Factory-fresh to lightly used. Premium owners maintain these weapons meticulously. Walnut may show minor handling marks or light contact wear on the stock wrist. Barrels remain mirror-polished. No rust, corrosion, or mechanical wear visible. Appears as a treasured sporting instrument rather than a field weapon.
